title: Yielding to a Block
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of yielding to a block in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply yielding to a block in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to detecting optional blocks and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Yielding to a Block through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding yielding to a block helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Yielding to a Block helps you reason about the yield keyword. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: The yield keyword. Then connect it to Passing values to blocks. The remaining syllabus points—Detecting optional blocks—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Yielding to a Block
content_blocks.code:
def around
  puts "start"
  yield
  puts "finish"
end
around { puts "work" }

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports yielding to a block. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for yielding to a block using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Detecting optional blocks), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain yielding to a block, identify its place in blocks, procs, lambdas, and closures, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
